results.question: What are the prerequisites for Deep Learning (TDIS22)?
results.expected_answer: 90 credits in Computer Engineering/Computer Science/Electrical Engineering or 150 credits from Computer Science and Engineering, plus completed Artificial Intelligence, Mathematics for Intelligent Systems and Machine Learning (7.5 credits each) or equivalent; English proficiency.
results.answer: To take Deep Learning (TDIS22), you need at least 90 credits within the major subject Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or Electrical Engineering (with relevant Computer Engineering courses), or equivalent, or at least 150 credits from the Computer Science and Engineering programme. You must also have completed Artificial Intelligence (7.5 credits), Mathematics for Intelligent Systems (7.5 credits), and Machine Learning (7.5 credits) or equivalents, plus proof of English proficiency. These rules come from the Deep Learning (TDIS22) syllabus only.

results.question: How is TARI29 graded?
results.expected_answer: 5, 4, 3 or U; final grade only after all assessments are completed.
results.answer: TARI29 (Artificial Intelligence, 7.5 credits, valid from 2025-09-01) is graded 5, 4, 3 or U. The final grade is based on a balanced set of assessments and is only issued after satisfactory completion of all assessments: the Examination (5 credits) and the Assignment (2.5 credits), each graded 5/4/3/U [1][2].

results.question: What grading scale does the Communication and Artificial Intelligence course use?
results.expected_answer: A, B, C, D, E, FX or F; A to E are passing grades.
results.answer: The Communication and Artificial Intelligence (LAIK15) course is graded on the scale A, B, C, D, E, FX or F, where A to E are passing grades [1]. Its group presentation element is graded U/G rather than on this scale [5].

results.question: What do I need before taking Mathematical Statistics?
results.expected_answer: General entry requirements and completed Single Variable Calculus, 7.5 credits, or equivalent.
results.answer: According to the syllabus for Mathematical Statistics (TMSK17), you need the general entry requirements and completed Single Variable Calculus, 7.5 credits (or the equivalent) [2]. This rule comes from TMSK17 only, so other courses may have different prerequisites.

results.question: How is the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence course examined?
results.expected_answer: Active participation in seminars and group discussions, and three assignments; graded 5, 4, 3 or U.
results.answer: The course is graded 5, 4, 3 or U. Examination consists of active participation in seminars and group discussions, plus three assignments. The first investigates an ethical challenge related to fairness in a practical case, and the second and third debate (for or against) a relevant ethical topic, one as a group presentation and one as a written assignment. The final grade is based on a balanced set of assessments and is issued only after all assessments are satisfactorily completed.

results.question: How is the final project in computer science examined?
results.expected_answer: Written report, oral presentation, opposition on another group's work, and mandatory elements; graded 5, 4, 3 or Fail.
results.answer: The question does not name a course, so there are two current versions. In Final Project Work in Computer Science (TEXT25, 2025), the course is examined through a written report, an oral presentation, and opposition to another group's report, and a grade is given only after all parts are passed [1]. In Final Project Work in Computer Science (TEXV23, 2024), it is examined through a written report, an oral presentation, review and discussion of another group's work, and fulfilment of mandatory elements, graded 5/4/3/U [3]. Other courses may differ.

results.question: Does the Deep Learning course include a project?
results.expected_answer: Yes: one project with tutoring and two project seminars (design and final presentation).
results.answer: Yes. Deep Learning (TDIS22) includes a project worth 5.5 credits, assessed through the project report and two presentations [1][5]. Deep Learning for PhD Students (FT3DLFP) also includes one project, with project tutoring and two project seminars [2]. Other courses may differ.

results.question: Which language is the Artificial Intelligence course TARI29 taught in?
results.expected_answer: English.
results.answer: The Artificial Intelligence course (TARI29) is taught in English. [1]

results.question: What topics does TARI29 cover?
results.expected_answer: Traditional AI and search, reasoning under uncertainty, evolutionary optimization, intelligent agents, game theory and minimax, Markov decision processes.
results.answer: TARI29 (Artificial Intelligence, 7.5 credits, current version valid from 2025-09-01) covers traditional AI (problem representation, production systems, search, planning, expert systems, automated reasoning, propositional and predicate logic, resolution), reasoning under uncertainty such as Bayesian inferencing, and programming an evolutionary optimization solution. It also covers intelligent agents, basic game theory with minimax, and agents for Markov decision processes [1][2].

results.question: What are the entry requirements for Mathematics for Intelligent Systems?
results.expected_answer: Bachelor's degree (180 credits) with at least 90 credits in Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Informatics, Information Systems, IT or Electrical Engineering, or equivalent, including at least 15 credits of mathematics.
results.answer: For Mathematics for Intelligent Systems (TMAR21), applicants need a bachelor's degree (180 ECTS) with at least 90 credits in Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Informatics, Information Systems, Information Technology or Electrical Engineering (with relevant computer engineering courses), or equivalent. The degree must include at least 15 credits in mathematics, and proof of English proficiency is required.

results.question: Can the credit requirements for the final project work in Computer Science (TEXV23) be waived?
results.expected_answer: The programme manager can grant an exemption from the points requirements, but not from the required Bachelor degree.
results.answer: Yes. For the Final Project Work in Computer Science (TEXV23), the programme manager can grant an exemption from the points requirements under Prerequisites [1]. No exemption will be made to the required Bachelor degree [1]. The prerequisites include passed second-cycle credits and mathematics credits from first cycle [4].

results.question: When can I start my final project work?
results.expected_answer: After the examiner's approval.
results.answer: You can start your final project work once the examiner has approved your registration form and project description [3][5]. The course syllabi for Final Project Work in Computer Science (TEXT25) [1], Production Systems (TEPV25) [2] and Product Development (TETT23) [4] also state that you may start after examiner approval, but other courses may differ. You must also meet the prerequisites in the course syllabus [3].

results.question: Which courses must I have taken before Intelligent Optimization and Problem Solving?
results.expected_answer: Artificial Intelligence, 7.5 credits, among the listed courses, plus 90 credits in Computer Engineering/Electrical Engineering or 150 credits from Computer Science and Engineering.
results.answer: To take Intelligent Optimization and Problem Solving, you need either at least 90 credits in Computer Engineering or Electrical Engineering (with relevant Computer Engineering courses), or equivalent [1]. Alternatively, you need at least 150 credits in Computer Science and Engineering, plus Artificial Intelligence (7.5 credits) and Knowledge Representation and the Semantic Web (7.5 credits), or equivalent [1]. You also must prove English proficiency [1].

results.question: How is the final grade decided in Deep Learning?
results.expected_answer: Graded 5, 4, 3 or Fail; project credits come from the report, two presentations and active participation in two seminars.
results.answer: In Deep Learning (TDIS22), the course is graded 5, 4, 3 or Fail, and the final grade is determined by the two presentations and the project report [1]. Project 1 (5.5 credits, graded 5/4/3/U) determines the final grade, but it is issued only when all course units are passed, including Assignments 1 and 2, which are graded U/G [2]. The project report grade reflects both the collaborative and the individual parts of the report [1].

results.question: What kind of teaching does Data Science Programming have?
results.expected_answer: Lectures, quizzes, assignments, workshops and tutoring, in English.
results.answer: Data Science Programming (TDPS22) is taught through lectures, quizzes, assignments, workshops and tutoring, and the teaching is conducted in English [1].

results.question: What happens if I am late to my exam?
results.expected_answer: Doors are closed and locked 10 minutes before the exam starts; be on site no later than 10 minutes before.
results.answer: If you arrive after the doors lock 10 minutes before the exam (08:50 AM or 01:50 PM), you will not be admitted at first and must wait for the second admission at 9:30 AM or 2:30 PM [2]. An invigilator will then check your ID, give short instructions, and tell you your seat number [1]. If you arrive more than 30 minutes late, you will not be allowed to take the exam, and no excuses are accepted [1].

results.question: How many days before an exam must I register?
results.expected_answer: No later than 10 days before; unregistered students cannot take the exam.
results.answer: I do not know based on the available documents.

results.question: Which IDs are accepted at exams?
results.expected_answer: Valid Swedish driver's license, Swedish passport, Swedish national ID card, or JU card marked Identity Card; valid foreign passports under conditions.
results.answer: Accepted IDs for exams are a valid Swedish driver's license, a valid Swedish passport, a valid Swedish national ID card, or a valid JU card marked "Identity Card" [1]. Foreign passports must be valid, plastic wrapped, and in English, French, or Spanish [1]. BankID and Freja eID+ are not accepted because they are not physical identification [1].

results.question: Can I identify myself with BankID at an exam?
results.expected_answer: No. BankID and Freja eID+ are not physical identification.
results.answer: No. BankID and Freja eID+ do not count as physical identification and are not accepted as valid ID during exams. You must show an accepted physical ID, such as a valid Swedish driver's license, passport, national ID card, or a JU card marked "Identity Card".

results.question: Can I bring snacks into the exam hall?
results.expected_answer: Food and drinks are allowed, but no nuts, smelly or smudging food, and no fragrances.
results.answer: Yes, you can bring food and drinks to the examination halls, but nuts or any food containing nuts, and food that smells or smudges, are not allowed. [1]

results.question: When am I allowed to leave the exam hall?
results.expected_answer: Not during the first 30 minutes.
results.answer: You may not leave the exam hall during the first 30 minutes [1]. After that, leaving for anything other than a restroom visit, or without an invigilator's permission, is treated as cancelling your exam [1][2]. Restroom visits must be logged on the restroom list, and if the restrooms are outside the hall, only one student may leave at a time [1].

results.question: How long does it take to get my exam results?
results.expected_answer: Results are reported via Ladok no later than 20 working days after the exam, except for special reasons.
results.answer: Exam results are normally notified to students through Ladok no later than 20 working days after the examination occasion. If special reasons exist, they may be notified later, but no later than 14 days before the next examination occasion for the course, and students must be told in writing.

results.question: Can I keep my student accommodation during a study break?
results.expected_answer: No.
results.answer: No. Under the consequences of a study break, the student is not allowed to keep student accommodation while on a study break [1].

results.question: What does a study break mean for my residence permit?
results.expected_answer: JU informs the Migration Agency, which revokes the residence permit, so the student must leave Sweden.
results.answer: An approved study break means Jönköping University informs the Swedish Migration Agency, which will revoke your residence permit, so you must leave Sweden [1]. Before applying, it is recommended that you meet your programme's study counsellor to understand these consequences [1].

results.question: What disciplinary measures can be taken against a student?
results.expected_answer: Warning, exclusion from examinations, and suspension; expulsion is also possible.
results.answer: Under the Disciplinary and Expulsion Committee's instructions, the disciplinary measures are warning, exclusion from examinations, and suspension [2]. Suspension may last up to six months in total, and exclusion from examinations for a continuous period of up to six months [2]. The Committee can also invoke expulsion, which means the student may not continue their education until further notice [2].

results.question: Which decisions can I appeal to the Board of Appeals?
results.expected_answer: Disciplinary Committee decisions (warning, suspension, expulsion) and listed faculty/school decisions.
results.answer: Under the current Board of Appeals list, you can appeal Disciplinary Committee warnings, suspensions, and expulsions, and faculty decisions such as rejecting an applicant for not meeting entry requirements, refusing exemptions or deferred enrolment, transferring credits, refusing a degree or course certificate (unless due to unpaid fees), withdrawing admission due to incorrect information, refusing exemption from a compulsory element, refusing leave from studies, or withdrawing a doctoral student's supervision [1][5]. You can also appeal refusals of tuition fee refunds based on special circumstances [2], and decisions subject to appeal under the Discrimination Act [1][4]. Disciplinary Committee decisions must be appealed in writing to the Committee within three weeks of the decision [4]. The Committee's instructions state that its expulsion decisions cannot be appealed, which conflicts with the list in [1], so check with the University.

results.question: How do I pay the application fee for a local admission?
results.expected_answer: To JU, by approved bank card (VISA/MasterCard) via the web payment system.
results.answer: For local admissions, the application fee is paid to JU, either by bank card (VISA/MasterCard) via the web-based payment solution in the online application form, or in another manner agreed with JU [1]. It must be paid no later than the deadline for supplementary information, and if you already paid the UHR fee for central admission, you must submit a receipt to JU [1].

results.question: What does § 5 of the disciplinary committee instructions say?
results.expected_answer: The disciplinary measures are warning, exclusion from examinations and suspension.
results.answer: Section § 5 lists the disciplinary measures as warning, exclusion from examinations and suspension. A warning is informed in writing, exclusion from examinations bars participation in University examinations for a stated continuous period of at most six months, and suspension bars attendance at classes, examinations and other education activities for periods totaling at most six months. Each decision must include its grounds.

results.question: What does section 2.15 of the education regulations say about grades?
results.expected_answer: Results are notified via Ladok within 20 working days of the examination.
results.answer: Section 2.15 (Betyg) requires that exam results be reported in Ladok no later than 20 working days after the exam, with written notice to students if there are special reasons for a delay. Feedback on examined elements must be offered no later than 14 days before the next ordinary exam for the course. Grade notifications must be issued in forms that protect students' legal rights and integrity and reach the correct student. Equal treatment under the Swedish Discrimination Act should be considered when designing examinations.

results.question: What are the TARI29 entry requirements?
results.expected_answer: Bachelor's degree (180 credits) with at least 90 credits in Computer Engineering, Computer Science or Electrical Engineering, or 150 credits from Computer Science and Engineering.
results.answer: Applicants need at least a bachelor's degree (180 ECTS) with at least 90 credits in Computer Engineering, Computer Science or Electrical Engineering (or equivalent), or 150 credits from Computer Science and Engineering. The degree must include at least 15 credits in mathematics, and proof of English proficiency is required. These rules come from the TARI29 Artificial Intelligence syllabus only [1].

results.question: What is LAIK15 about?
results.expected_answer: Media and communication and artificial intelligence, including representations of AI and generative AI in media.
results.answer: LAIK15, Communication and Artificial Intelligence (7.5 credits, first-cycle), covers research perspectives on AI, representations of AI, and generative AI as a tool for producing texts. It also addresses the impact of AI in different media and communication contexts, including its opportunities and limitations [3][4][1][2]. Students learn to describe and explain these topics in relation to media and communication traditions [5].

results.question: Is TDPS22 taught in English?
results.expected_answer: Yes.
results.answer: Yes, Data Science Programming (TDPS22) is taught in English, according to the current 2025 version of the course syllabus [1].

results.question: What does § 28 of the disciplinary committee instructions allow?
results.expected_answer: A decision may always be appealed to the Board of Appeals if it contravenes the Discrimination Act.
results.answer: Section 28 allows a decision of the Disciplinary and Expulsion Committee to always be appealed to the Board of Appeals, on the ground that the decision contravenes specified sections of the Discrimination Act (2008:567). The passage is cut off, so the full list of sections cannot be confirmed.

results.question: How many re-exam attempts do I get?
results.expected_answer: Re-exam rules are set per course; the answer must say which course(s) its rule comes from.
results.answer: Each examination is guaranteed at least three attempts in total, including the regular attempt, so you are entitled to at least two re-examinations [1][2][3][4][5]. This rule appears in the current syllabi for L1REAR, LHMR25, LLLR24, L2LDAS and LMKR24, and other courses may differ. If you have failed the same exam three times, you can ask for the next attempt to be graded by a new examiner, and the associate dean of education decides on that request [1][2][3][4][5].

results.question: Can the credit requirements for the final project work be waived?
results.expected_answer: Depends on the programme; usually the programme manager can grant an exemption, but not from the Bachelor degree. Must name the course(s).
results.answer: Yes, in these courses the credit requirements under Prerequisites can be waived. In Final Project Work in Computer Science (TEXT25), Final Project Work in Informatics (TEIT22), and Final Project Work in Built Environment (TEBV24), the programme manager can grant the exemption, but no exemption is made for the required Bachelor degree [1][4][5]. In Final Project Work in Informatics (TWIP17), the course coordinator can give the exemption [2], and in Final Project Work in Production Systems (TEUT23), the programme manager can grant it under separate instructions [3].
